$schema: binding sweep for the two duplicate 1px width variables in the SAMAVESH Figma library

coverage.note: The four separator pages report children: 0, so they can hold no bindings. Every other page was walked individually — batching returns partial trees, and a partial tree here is a FALSE NEGATIVE on a delete decision.

canonical.name: ref/border/width/sm
canonical.note: The real one. Code-defined, exported by the pipeline, correct grammar. Prefer `control/border/width`, which aliases it and says what the edge is for.

duplicates.name: ref/border-width/hairline
duplicates.verdict: STILL UNDELETABLE — but for a different, precise reason
duplicates.why: Down from 242 to 79 after the Divider rebind. Every one of the 79 remaining is a documentation-frame BORDER, not a divider: strokeTopWeight / strokeBottomWeight / strokeLeftWeight / strokeRightWeight on Do and Don't cards, on doc `row` frames, and on one `close` frame. Layout Grid 51, Navbar 12, Portal Login 8, Accessibility Bar 8.
duplicates.howToRetire: These are generic 1px borders and there is NO published Tier-2 border-width token to move them to. control/border/width is scope-correct (STROKE_FLOAT) but says 'interactive control', which a documentation card is not — binding them there would be the by-convenience mistake this whole exercise exists to avoid. The clean fix is a semantic border/width/* Tier-2 token; until that exists, hairline stays. It is hidden from publishing, so it is not offered to designers in the meantime.

duplicates.name: cmp/divider/width
duplicates.verdict: RESOLVED — deleted and replaced by a code-backed token of the same name
duplicates.why: Nothing in the library binds it — zero hits across all 69 pages. It was created on 2026-08-18 (id 55677:*, among the newest in the file) and never wired up: the Divider component binds `ref/border-width/hairline` directly instead. It is PUBLISHED, so it does appear in designers' pickers as a plausible-looking choice that no code token backs.
duplicates.alternativeToDeleting: If a Divider component token is actually wanted, define `cmp/divider/width` in packages/tokens/src/component.json and let the exporter own it — the exporter now routes cmp/* by type, so it would land in Space and upsert onto this same id, preserving it.

outcome.cmp/divider/width: DELETED (id 55677:37371, the hand-made orphan, 0 bindings) and RECREATED as a code-backed token (id 55703:695). It is now defined in packages/tokens/src/component.json, owned by the exporter, and carries var(--sa-cmp-divider-width) with WIDTH_HEIGHT|STROKE_FLOAT scope. `divider` was registered in grammar.mjs COMPONENT — which failed LOUDLY, unlike the exporter's old silent drop.
outcome.Divider variants: All six COMPONENT variants (Orientation x Tone) plus 3 page instances rebound from ref/border-width/hairline to cmp/divider/width. Same value, 1px, zero visual change.
outcome.instancePropagation: 233 of the 242 hairline bindings were Divider INSTANCES. Rebinding the six mains carried 163 of them automatically — Tabs 3/3, Side Sheet 2/2, Accessibility Bar 39/47, Navbar 48/60, Portal Login 62/70. Instances follow their main unless they carry an explicit override, which is exactly why the mains are done first.
outcome.whyControlBorderWidthWasRejected: The original recommendation was to rebind to control/border/width. On inspection that was wrong twice: it is scoped STROKE_FLOAT only, while the Divider binds its thickness to WIDTH/HEIGHT (it is a rectangle, not a stroke); and it means 'the border width of an interactive control', which a divider is not.
